title: Confession and Autopsy
premise: Retired detective Orsen Oyelaran, now barely keeping their bookshop afloat, receives two letters the same morning: one confessing to the unsolved murder of Ada Voss twenty years ago, and one promising that 'the rest is coming.' The confession names Orsen's old partner as the killer — but the handwriting belongs to someone who should be dead. As the anniversary dinner approaches and more letters arrive, Orsen reopens the case everyone swore was closed, discovering that Ada's death was covered up by the very people who investigated it. In the end, Orsen must choose between turning in the living confessor — the person they've come to love — or letting justice die quietly at an anniversary toast.
about_author: Emrys Kavanagh is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent fifteen years transcribing confessions before writing any of their own. They live above a secondhand bookshop in a coastal town that appears in none of their novels, which they insist is a coincidence.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Morning
chapters.summary: Orsen Oyelaran opens the shop to find two letters: a detailed confession to Ada Voss's murder signed by their former partner, Detective Rell Hargrove, and a second unsigned note promising 'the rest is coming.' POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine — the past knocking on glass.

chapters.title: The Case That Wasn't Cold
chapters.summary: Orsen digs out their private files on the Voss case, closed twenty years ago as an accident. The confession's details match evidence only investigators saw. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: professional pride curdling into dread as memory sharpens.

chapters.title: Hargrove Answers the Door
chapters.summary: Orsen confronts Rell Hargrove, who denies writing anything and seems genuinely frightened — not of guilt, but of being named. He reveals he received his own letter last week. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: suspicion of an old friend, loyalty cracking.

chapters.title: The Handwriting That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: A graphologist friend confirms the confession was written by Maren Voss — Ada's daughter, who drowned herself a year after her mother's death. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: vertigo; the dead are testifying.

chapters.title: Third Letter
chapters.summary: A third letter arrives describing the night of Ada's death from inside the house, including a detail about a broken teacup no report ever mentioned. It ends: 'Ask Orsen. They were there.' POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: exposure — the writer knows them intimately.

chapters.title: What I Did That Night
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Orsen's first-person memory: the young detective's failure to follow a lead on the Voss case because of orders from above. POV: Orsen (past). Emotional beat: shame resurfacing; complicity acknowledged.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Committee
chapters.summary: The town prepares its twentieth-anniversary memorial dinner for Ada Voss, chaired by Councilman Dree Hale — once the lead investigator. Orsen notices Hale flinch at the word 'confession.' POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: civic warmth masking rot.

chapters.title: Maren's Room
chapters.summary: Orsen breaks into the sealed Voss house and finds Maren's preserved bedroom, journals, and drafts of the letters — written over years, addressed to Orsen alone. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: grief and intimacy with a stranger who knew everything.

chapters.title: Someone Is Sending Them
chapters.summary: The journals stop two years ago; the recent postmarks are local. Someone alive is mailing Maren's words. Orsen stakes out the postbox and glimpses a figure in a green coat. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: hunter becoming hunted.

chapters.title: Duty Calls, Love Answers
chapters.summary: Inspector Sefa Onyekwere, reopening the file officially, warns Orsen off — then shares a drink and an old tenderness resurfaces. Duty demands Orsen hand over the letters; love makes them hesitate. POV: alternating Orsen/Sefa. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: The Teacup Testimony
chapters.summary: Orsen matches the teacup detail to a suppressed forensic note proving Ada died hours before the official time — meaning someone with access altered the record. Only three people could have. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: the cover-up acquires faces.

chapters.title: Green Coat
chapters.summary: Orsen corners the letter-sender: it is Ivy Voss, Maren's twin sister, presumed relocated, actually hiding in town. She confesses she's finishing what Maren started — and that there are four letters left. POV: Ivy. Emotional beat: fury braided with mourning.

chapters.title: Four Letters Left
chapters.summary: Ivy gives Orsen one letter early: it names Councilman Hale as the man who ordered the timeline altered. Orsen realizes each remaining letter will detonate before the dinner. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: countdown begins.

chapters.title: Hale's Glass Raised Early
chapters.summary: Orsen confronts Hale privately; he offers Orsen money and a seat on the memorial committee to bury the letters. His charm slips into threat. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: temptation and contempt in the same handshake.

chapters.title: Sefa Reads Everything
chapters.summary: Sefa discovers Orsen withheld evidence and gives them until the dinner to explain — duty and love now openly at war. Orsen chooses honesty, showing her Maren's journals. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: betrayal, then fragile alliance.

chapters.title: The Fifth Letter Burns
chapters.summary: A fire at the bookshop destroys the fifth letter and nearly Orsen. Arson points to someone protecting Hale — or impersonating him. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: escalation; the case turns violent.

chapters.title: Who Taught Maren to Drown
chapters.summary: Re-examining Maren's death, Orsen finds her suicide note was forged — she was silenced after learning the truth. The sixth letter, delivered unburned, says so in Maren's own hand. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: rage crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Toast
chapters.summary: Orsen, Sefa, and Ivy assemble the full chain: Hale altered the record, Hargrove was framed by the confession's timing, and Maren paid with her life. They plan to expose it publicly at the dinner. POV: rotating trio. Emotional beat: quiet before the storm, bonds forged.

chapters.title: Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: At the memorial, as glasses rise, the seventh letter is read aloud by Ivy. Hale denies everything until Sefa produces the suppressed forensic note. The room turns. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: climax — justice spoken where lies were toasted.

chapters.title: Confession, Second Draft
chapters.summary: Cornered, Hale confesses — and reveals the original confession's cruel twist: Maren wrote it believing Hargrove guilty, and Ivy has been sending a dead woman's mistake. Orsen must decide whether truth still counts when it's wrong. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: devastating complication.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Hargrove, cleared but ruined, forgives Orsen; Hale is arrested on evidence Sefa can legally use. Ivy faces charges for harassment and arson, and Orsen refuses to let her take the fall alone, testifying to context and mercy. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved — both kept, both cost something.

chapters.title: Closing the Bookshop Case
chapters.summary: Months later, Orsen places Maren's journals in the shop window, sells a book to Sefa, and finally writes their own account — closing the one case everyone swore was closed. The last line mirrors the first letter. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: peace earned, memory honored.
